claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the circular 'X' logo and the specific perforated grill design of an Xbox One S.
Photo 0 explicitly shows a disc drive slot visible on the front, which is absent on the All-Digital Edition.
Relative size cannot be confirmed without a reference object or measurements, though the 'Slim' profile is noted in Photo 1.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty or jammed.
risks.proof: A video showing a disc being inserted, read, and ejected.
risks.if_unproven: As a console with a broken disc drive.

risks.risk: The HDMI port may be damaged or non-functional (common on this model).
risks.proof: A video showing the console booting to the dashboard on a TV screen.

risks.risk: Internal storage may be the base 500GB rather than 1TB.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'Settings > System > Storage' screen.

risks.risk: The console may be banned from Xbox Network (Live).
risks.proof: A video showing the console successfully signing into an Xbox profile while connected to the internet.

proof_requests: Video of the console powered on and connected to a TV showing the home menu.
Photo of the storage settings screen showing total capacity.
Video of a game disc being inserted and recognized by the system.
Photos of the console with the clear plastic wrap removed to check for scratches or heat damage.
response.reason: The witness confirmed the item is an Xbox One S with a physical disc drive, directly contradicting the seller's 'All-Digital' description. It will be priced as a standard Xbox One S in unknown functional condition.
